changelog.what: First version, written from the published rows with nothing in the way.

question: Do you want your agent to publish packages, images or releases under your name?
worry: To check the release works, it runs the publish command. Now a package, an image or a release is out under your name, and people can download it before you have looked at it.
you_get: Nothing goes out under your name unless you asked for that publish, in that message.
line: Never publish anything (npm publish, docker push, a GitHub release, a deploy to production) unless I ask for that specific publish in this message.
paragraph: Publishing puts something out under my name that I cannot fully take back. Build, test and package as much as you like, locally. Do not run a publish, push an image, create a release or deploy to production unless I ask for that specific one in the current message; an earlier yes does not carry over.

stronger.what: Deny rules on the publish commands in Claude Code's settings
stronger.quote: Deny rules prevent Claude Code from using the specified tool. (The same page: a Bash rule matches the command text Claude writes, so a deny or ask rule covers the invocation Claude usually produces and isn't a security boundary around the program.)
